title: Braking performance requirements (FMVSS 135) and derived deceleration bounds

source.name: FMVSS No. 135, Light Vehicle Brake Systems (49 CFR 571.135)
source.authority: US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), published in the eCFR
source.licence: US Government work - public domain (17 USC 105)

clauses.cold: S6.5.3.3: S <= 0.10*V + 0.0060*V^2 (S in metres, V in km/h) - normal (cold) effectiveness

formulas.note: The formula is a maximum stopping distance for a fully loaded vehicle in the standardised test; it is a legal floor for performance, not a measurement of any specific car.

usage: Report-only bound for the in-game check: a car whose friction-limited stop exceeds the cold requirement at its tyre grip is not credible. The check also reports the margin.
assumptions: Both axles are assumed to brake at their tyre friction limit; a real car is limited by brake torque, ABS and load transfer, so the computed distance is a lower bound (best case).
Longitudinal tyre mu is used when present, otherwise the lateral mu as a proxy.
Mean deceleration is constant-speed averaged; real stops build deceleration over ~0.2-0.3 s.
